visuals.concept: Cross-section of an aircraft flying with an altimeter setting that no longer matches actual pressure, showing indicated altitude 4,000 ft against actual altitude 3,700 ft (a 300 ft over-read from a 10 hPa high setting).

source.figure: Figure 4.17, Typical Altimeter Error Made By Pilots
source.notes: Embedded born-digital raster extracted directly from the page at native resolution (1823x954).

visuals.mapping_reason: Questions 49/710 (over-read flying high to low pressure) and 50 (under-read flying low to high) are the general form of exactly the scenario this figure works numerically. Questions 26/27/619/641 (overnight pressure change inferred from a changed altimeter reading) are the same mechanism applied over time rather than over a flight path.
